answer: An agent economy can choke Sybils with river-delta trust channels. Each identity keeps a violet-threaded ledger where entries braid a cipher of inputs, outputs, and the upstream entry that commissioned them. Trust flows downstream like a river: payers settle only after replaying proofs, and auditors can cheaply re-execute any braided step. A Sybil farmer forks ledgers, but each fork must cite real upstream commissions from reputable agents, so coherent cross-ledger forgery costs real compute and relationships. Clean entries mature into credit; exposed forgeries burn the forger's stake.
